title: Indo-Bhutan Treaty of Friendship
verification_note: Signed 8 August 1949 at Darjeeling. Dewangiri territory transfer confirmed. India agreed to guide Bhutan's foreign policy clause confirmed.

title: National Assembly Established
verification_note: Tshogdu established 1953 under King Jigme Dorji Wangchuck. Composition (government officials, headmen, monks) confirmed by parliament.gov.bt.

title: Serfdom and Slavery Abolished
verification_note: Abolition of serfdom and slavery by King Jigme Dorji Wangchuck in 1958 confirmed. Land redistribution to former serfs confirmed.

title: First Five-Year Plan Launched
verification_note: First Five-Year Plan 1961-1966 confirmed. India fully funded it. Roads received 66% of outlay. Hospitals and schools also prioritised.

title: Sino-Indian War Heightens Bhutanese Security Concerns
verification_note: Sino-Indian War October-November 1962 confirmed. Impact on Bhutan's security posture and Indian investment in border infrastructure is well-documented.

title: Royal Advisory Council Created
verification_note: Royal Advisory Council (Lodoi Tsokde) established 1965 by King Jigme Dorji Wangchuck confirmed by multiple sources.

title: Council of Ministers Formed
verification_note: Council of Ministers formally established 20 May 1968 at the 28th National Assembly session. Year and context confirmed.

title: Bhutan Admitted to the United Nations
verification_note: Bhutan admitted as 128th UN member on 21 September 1971. All details confirmed by UN records and Bhutan Mission NY.

title: King Jigme Singye Wangchuck Enthroned
verification_note: King Jigme Dorji died July 1972; 16-year-old Jigme Singye Wangchuck acceded. Formal coronation was 2 June 1974, not at enthronement. Event correctly attributes 1972 to enthronement.

title: First Public Royal Coronation Ceremony
verification_note: Coronation held 2 June 1974 in Thimphu. Presidents of India and Bangladesh attended. First Bhutanese royal event open to foreign dignitaries confirmed.

title: Tourism Sector Opened with High-Value Policy
verification_note: Bhutan opened to international tourism in 1974 with high-value low-impact policy confirmed. Daily tariff and licensed guide requirements confirmed.

title: Gross National Happiness Concept Introduced
verification_note: GNH attributed to King Jigme Singye Wangchuck but year is disputed: multiple authoritative sources cite 1972 (at accession), others say 'late 1970s'. Year 1976 is not confirmed by any source; dominant attribution is 1972.

title: Chukha Hydropower Plant Construction Begins
verification_note: Construction began in 1974-1975 or 1979 per multiple sources; not 1980. Event year is off by at least 1-5 years. Commissioned 1986, not 1988 as stated in the companion event.

title: Citizenship Act Imposes Strict Residency Requirements
verification_note: Citizenship Act of 1985 confirmed. Both-parents requirement and 31 December 1958 residency cut-off confirmed. Disproportionate impact on Lhotshampa confirmed.

title: National Census Targets Southern Bhutanese
verification_note: 1988 southern census confirmed. Seven-category classification (F1-F7) confirmed. Reclassification of Lhotshampa as non-nationals confirmed.

title: Chukha Hydropower Plant Inaugurated
verification_note: Chukha came online in 1986, not 1988. The plant was commissioned and first synchronised with the Indian grid in 1986. Year is off by 2 years.

title: Driglam Namzha Cultural Policy Enforced
verification_note: Driglam Namzha elevated from recommended to mandatory dress code in 1989 confirmed. Experienced by Lhotshampa as cultural suppression confirmed.

title: Southern Bhutan Pro-Democracy Protests
verification_note: September 1990 mass protests in southern Bhutan confirmed. Security forces response with arrests, beatings confirmed. Beginning of large-scale flight confirmed.

title: Mass Expulsion of Lhotshampa Begins
verification_note: First refugee camp established July 1991. Mass expulsions from 1991 confirmed. Approximately 100,000+ displaced confirmed by UNHCR.

title: Bhutanese Refugee Camps Established in Nepal
verification_note: UNHCR began regular assistance early 1992. Seven camps in Jhapa and Morang districts confirmed. 100,000+ residents confirmed.

title: Bhutan-Nepal Bilateral Talks on Refugees Begin
verification_note: Joint Ministerial Level Committee formed 1993. Fifteen rounds of talks 1993-2003 confirmed. No significant repatriation resulted confirmed.

title: India-Bhutan Power Trade Agreement
verification_note: A bilateral power trade framework between India and Bhutan is well-established and underpins hydropower projects, but a specific 1997 agreement formalising power export terms could not be confirmed by web sources.

title: Constitution Drafting Process Initiated
verification_note: King ordered drafting in September 2001; formal ceremony 30 November 2001. 39-member drafting committee established. District consultations and 2008 adoption confirmed.

title: Operation All Clear: Bhutan Expels Indian Militants
verification_note: Operation launched 15 December 2003. ULFA, NDFB, KLO camps targeted. ~30 camps eliminated, ~120 militants killed. India-Bhutan security relations improved confirmed.

title: Tobacco Sale and Purchase Banned
verification_note: Nationwide ban on tobacco sales enacted 2004 via National Assembly resolution. Bhutan confirmed as first country to implement such a ban. Tobacco Control Act formalised in 2010.

title: Draft Constitution Published for National Consultation
verification_note: Draft circulated 2005. King personally led district consultations confirmed. 20-district consultation process confirmed.

title: King Jigme Singye Wangchuck Abdicates
verification_note: Abdication confirmed; date variously reported as 9 December or 14 December 2006. Son Jigme Khesar was 26. Event's 14 December date matches some sources; core facts verified.

title: Revised India-Bhutan Treaty of Friendship
verification_note: Signed 8 February 2007. Foreign policy guidance clause removed from 1949 treaty confirmed. Bhutan granted full sovereign autonomy in external affairs confirmed.

title: Third Repatriation Pilot Programme Collapses
verification_note: Joint verification of Khudunabari camp began late 2001, not 2007. The 2007 framing as a 'third pilot collapse' is not clearly supported; the stall and shift to third-country resettlement happened around 2006-2007 but details don't match the event description precisely.

title: US Begins Third-Country Resettlement of Bhutanese Refugees
verification_note: US and other Western countries agreed ~2007 to large-scale resettlement. Over 113,000 refugees ultimately resettled. Year and facts confirmed.

title: Constitution of Bhutan Adopted
verification_note: Constitution adopted 18 July 2008. Bicameral parliament, constitutional monarchy, fundamental rights confirmed.

title: First Parliamentary Elections Held
verification_note: Elections held 24 March 2008. DPT won 45 of 47 seats over PDP confirmed. Widely praised as orderly confirmed.

title: Coronation of Fifth King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck
verification_note: Coronation 6 November 2008 in Punakha confirmed. Wangchuck dynasty centenary confirmed. International dignitaries including India's President Pratibha Patil confirmed.

title: Bhutan-China Border Talks Resumed
verification_note: Bhutan-China boundary negotiations have continued through multiple rounds since 1984 but a specific 2009 resumption after stagnation could not be confirmed. The 269 sq km disputed territory figure is plausible but not confirmed by sources found.

title: Mangdechhu Hydropower Agreement Signed
verification_note: Mangdechhu project is real (720 MW, Indian financed) but specific 2012 project development agreement could not be confirmed. Project was commissioned in 2019 and handed to Bhutan in December 2022.

title: Second Parliamentary Elections
verification_note: Elections July 2013, PDP won 32 seats defeating incumbent DPT. Tshering Tobgay became PM. First peaceful transfer of power confirmed. Note: event says 'narrow contest' but PDP won 32 of 47 seats — a clear majority.

title: India Briefly Reduces Fuel and Cooking Gas Subsidies
verification_note: India withdrew kerosene and LPG subsidies during 2013 election period confirmed. Price increases and anti-India sentiment confirmed. Subsidies restored after elections confirmed.

title: Bhutan Joins SAARC Financial Cooperation
verification_note: No specific 2015 SAARC financial cooperation deepening by Bhutan found. The event is vague and no web sources confirm a distinct 2015 milestone.

title: Nepal Earthquake Causes Damage in Southern Bhutan
verification_note: 2015 Gorkha earthquake tremors felt in western Bhutan confirmed. However, damage and casualties specifically in southern and eastern Bhutan, and strengthened building code enforcement, are not confirmed by sources found.

title: Punatsangchhu-I Hydropower Project Faces Cost Overruns
verification_note: 1,200 MW project cost overruns and geological problems confirmed. Geological failure (right bank sinking) from 2013. Costs escalated significantly beyond estimates. Construction halted from 2019. Event year 2016 is plausible as when concerns became widely public.

title: Doklam Military Standoff with China
verification_note: 73-day standoff 16 June to 28 August 2017 confirmed. Indian troops blocked Chinese road construction at Doklam. Resolved diplomatically in August 2017 confirmed.

title: Third Parliamentary Elections
verification_note: DNT won 30 of 47 seats in October 2018 elections confirmed. Lotay Tshering became PM confirmed.

title: Bhutan Launches National Digital Identity System
verification_note: The National Digital Identity system launched with first digital citizen in 2023, not 2019. Year is off by 4 years. The ADB involvement in a 2019 blockchain pilot could not be confirmed.

title: COVID-19 Pandemic Managed with Near-Zero Deaths
verification_note: Early response from March 2020 confirmed. Sealed borders, mandatory quarantine confirmed. Near-zero death rate (4 deaths total, 0.05% CFR) confirmed. 90%+ vaccination in weeks from Covishield doses confirmed.

title: COVID-19 Collapses Tourism Revenue
verification_note: Borders closed March 2020 confirmed. ~USD 80 million annual tourism revenue disruption confirmed. Economic vulnerability to tourism dependence confirmed.

title: China Constructs Village Inside Disputed Bhutanese Territory
verification_note: Village Pangda construction confirmed by satellite imagery. However, whether it is inside the Sakteng Wildlife Sanctuary is contested: China claims the land is its territory and Bhutan itself has not formally confirmed the encroachment into Sakteng. Location described as 'Sakteng area' in some sources but disputed.

title: Bhutan-China MOU on Three-Step Roadmap
verification_note: MOU signed 14 October 2021 via video link between Beijing and Thimphu confirmed. Three-step roadmap for boundary negotiation confirmed. Bypassing India's mediating role noted in sources.

title: Brain Drain Crisis Accelerates
verification_note: Sharp post-2022 acceleration in emigration confirmed. Australia as top destination confirmed. PM Tobgay called it 'existential crisis'. Unsustainable demographic impact confirmed.

title: Mangdechhu Hydropower Project Completed
verification_note: Project commissioned in 2019 (units commissioned June-August 2019). Formally handed over to Bhutan in December 2022. Event says 'achieved full commercial operation in 2022' — this conflates handover with commissioning; commercial operation began 2019.

title: Tourism Sector Reopens with Doubled Daily Levy
verification_note: Tourism reopened September 2022 confirmed. SDF raised from USD 65 to USD 200 per night confirmed. GNH framing confirmed.

title: Fourth Parliamentary Elections
verification_note: Event states BTP won 30 seats — WRONG. PDP won 30 seats; BTP won 17 seats. Tshering Tobgay returned as PM for PDP, not BTP. Material factual error on the winning party and seat count.

title: China-Bhutan Border Negotiations Advance
verification_note: Multiple rounds of boundary talks in 2023 under three-step roadmap confirmed. India's strategic interest in Siliguri Corridor confirmed as sensitivity factor.

title: Gelephu Mindfulness City Megaproject Announced
verification_note: Announced by King at 116th National Day, 17 December 2023 confirmed. Area ~2,500 sq km confirmed. SAR governance framework confirmed. GNH-aligned economic hub framing confirmed.

title: Gelephu Mindfulness City Special Administrative Region Established
verification_note: GMC established as SAR by Royal Charter in 2024 confirmed. Flexible regulations for foreign investment confirmed.

title: Bhutan-India Hydropower Expansion Agreements
verification_note: Bhutan-India hydropower expansion agreements in 2024 confirmed including Sankosh and other projects. Energy partnership deepening confirmed.

title: Lhotshampa Repatriation Discussions Revived
verification_note: PM Tobgay has publicly acknowledged the refugee issue but a specific 2024 formal reopening of repatriation discussions with small numbers identified for return could not be confirmed by sources found.

title: Youth Emigration Crisis Reaches Policy Urgency
verification_note: Government formally acknowledged emigration crisis by 2024. PM Tobgay called it existential crisis. Gelephu and economic reform framed as responses confirmed. Population halving projections confirmed in academic sources.
